Subject: SIG/CAIQ: IR runbook walkthrough + artifacts needed for audit

Mina / Marissa —

Thanks for taking this quickly. FirstWave is doing a SIG/CAIQ evidence collection for an internal audit the week of July 8 and we need to confirm your IR artifacts and redaction approach for an incident we engaged on May 12. Specifically we need:

- A short (30–45 min) IR runbook walkthrough focused on detection -> containment -> evidence export steps.
- A sample of sanitized artifacts (redacted logs + packet capture summary) to validate PII/credential redaction.
- A one-page summary (postmortem-style) we can share with our audit team that describes scope, timeline, and mitigations applied.

Time is tight — can you confirm availability for a walkthrough this week and whether you can provide a sanitized artifact sample (redacted) by EOD Friday? We will include our third-party forensics partner (dlt-incident@thirdpartyforensics.io) for alignment.

Attachments: none on this message.

Elena Morales

Elena —

Thanks and understood. We can do a focused 30-minute walkthrough and provide a sanitized artifact sample. Proposed plan:

1) Walkthrough: today 15:30 PDT / 22:30 UTC (30 min) — we will cover detection signals we use, containment playbook, evidence export steps, and redaction controls.
2) Sanitized sample: we will deliver a tarball with redacted logs + packet-summary by 2028-07-03 EOD. The sample will include a redaction manifest that lists all redactions (types and counts).
3) Postmortem one-pager: we will provide a concise timeline and mitigations doc following the walkthrough; target 2028-07-05.

We have a short runbook excerpt attached for preview; it includes the commands we run for evidence export (sanitized) and our redaction policy notes. For clarity: we will not share raw PCAPs with PII — only summarized, redacted artifacts that meet typical banking audit requirements. If you need raw data under an NDA and approved redaction plan we can discuss a controlled transfer.

Attached: runbook_excerpt.pdf (excerpt, contains playbook steps and evidence export checklist)

I will host the call; Karthik will be available to answer technical questions about log exports. If that time doesn't work, propose alternatives and we'll adjust.

Best,

15:30 PDT works for us. Quick clarification ahead of the call so we can prepare the audit checklist:

- For the redaction manifest: can you include sample hashes (sha256) for exported files and an abbreviated mapping that explains why a redaction was applied (e.g., PIIs removed, tokenized, truncated)? We only need examples for the sample set.
- For packet summaries: please include the session metadata (timestamps, src/dst IPs redacted to class, protocol, and bytes) and an anonymized indicator of whether credentials were observed.
- Scope: the incident to which these artifacts relate is the May 12 authentication spike affecting 0.2% of tokens (FirstWave ticket FW-20280512). We need a postmortem paragraph referencing that scope.

Also copying our forensics partner so they can confirm if they need any additional context ahead of the walkthrough.

Elena

Elena —

Appreciate the quick coordination. Per the walkthrough (recording link saved to shared Drive) and follow-up work, we've attached the sanitized sample set and the redaction manifest. Summary (post-walkthrough):

- Timeline & scope: Redwood observed an authentication anomaly on 2028-05-12 between 03:24–03:56 UTC affecting ~0.2% of tokens issued to FirstWave. Containment occurred within 18 minutes of detection via automated throttling and token revocation.
- Artifacts delivered: sanitized_artifacts_sample.tar.gz (contains redacted logs, packet-summary.csv, and example event-extracts), forensic_summary_redacted.pdf (high-level forensics summary with attacker hypothesis redacted), redaction_manifest.csv (maps redacted fields, counts, and redaction rationale).
- Redaction approach: listwise redaction for PII (names, email addresses), IP address truncation to /16, token IDs tokenized with non-reversible hash; sensitive stack traces redacted at line level. Manifest includes example sha256 checksums for each exported file.
- SIG/CAIQ mapping: we've added an audit note linking the delivered artifacts to SIG control rows A1.2 / IR-1 / IR-3 in the shared Drive doc (link below).

Next steps:
- Elena / FirstWave audit team: review the sample and confirm whether the redaction level is acceptable for your auditors (reply to this thread).
- If raw, unredacted data is required under an approved transfer and NDA, open a secure transfer request with Redwood Legal (we will need an approved redaction plan and Data Processing Addendum).

Attachments: sanitized_artifacts_sample.tar.gz, forensic_summary_redacted.pdf, redaction_manifest.csv
Drive: https://drive.redwood.example.com/teams/security/FirstWave-SIG-CAIQ-2028 (permissions: FirstWave-sig-audit@firstwavebank.com)
